# package scanner

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/scanner"
```

Package scanner is the originator (scanner) of EtherNet/IP implicit I/O connections: it opens Class 1 (or Class 0) connections to a target's assemblies with Forward\_Open over a client session, exchanges their data cyclically over UDP, detects their timeout and, when asked to, reopens them.

	c, _ := client.Dial(ctx, "192.168.1.10")
	s, _ := scanner.New(c)
	io, _ := s.Open(ctx, scanner.IOConfig{
		ConfigInstance: 151, OutputInstance: 150, InputInstance: 100,
		OutputSize: 32, InputSize: 32, RPI: 10 * time.Millisecond,
	})
	io.SetOutput(out)
	in, run, at := io.Input()

The scanner's I/O endpoint listens on UDP port 2222 by default, the port targets send to; WithLocalAddr picks another, which Forward\_Open then announces in a Sockaddr Info item (not every target honours it). O->T data goes to the target's address, at the port the target's Sockaddr Info O->T item names (2222 without one).

#### func (IO) Close

```go
func (io *IO) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close stops the exchange and closes the connection with Forward\_Close (bounded by ctx). Close is idempotent.

#### func (IO) Done

```go
func (io *IO) Done() <-chan struct{}
```

Done is closed when the connection ends: by Close, or by a timeout without Reconnect.

#### func (IO) Err

```go
func (io *IO) Err() error
```

Err returns why the connection ended or last failed, or nil.

#### func (IO) Info

```go
func (io *IO) Info() ethernetip.ConnectionInfo
```

Info returns the connection's IDs, triad and actual intervals.

#### func (IO) Input

```go
func (io *IO) Input() ([]byte, bool, time.Time)
```

Input returns a copy of the last input (T->O) data, whether it said run, and when it arrived; zero time before the first.

#### func (IO) SetOutput

```go
func (io *IO) SetOutput(data []byte) error
```

SetOutput sets the output (O->T) data, sent from the next interval on. It must be exactly OutputSize octets.

#### func (IO) SetRun

```go
func (io *IO) SetRun(run bool)
```

SetRun sets the run/idle state the output carries (formats with the 32-bit header). New connections start in run.

#### func (IO) State

```go
func (io *IO) State() ethernetip.State
```

State returns the connection's state.

#### func (IO) Stats

```go
func (io *IO) Stats() implicit.Stats
```

Stats returns the counters of the current implicit connection.

### type IOConfig

```go
type IOConfig struct {
	// ConfigInstance is the configuration assembly, 0 for none. The
	// connection path always names it (instance 0 when there is none), as
	// the other originators do; ConfigData, when set, is sent in the
	// connection path.
	ConfigInstance uint32
	ConfigData     []byte
	// OutputInstance is the O->T connection point (the target's output or
	// heartbeat assembly); InputInstance the T->O point (its input
	// assembly).
	OutputInstance uint32
	InputInstance  uint32
	// OutputSize and InputSize are the sizes of the application data,
	// without sequence count and header.
	OutputSize int
	InputSize  int
	// RPI is the requested packet interval of both directions; OTRPI and
	// TORPI, when set, replace it per direction.
	//
	// The target answers with the actual packet intervals (APIs), which
	// the connection then uses and [IO.Info] reports; they may differ from
	// the RPIs. Open refuses the reply with ErrProtocol, and closes the
	// connection again, when the T->O API is 0 (no consumption timeout)
	// or the O->T API is below a quarter of the O->T RPI or below 100 µs
	// (the O->T RPI itself when that is shorter), so that the scanner
	// never produces more than four times as often as asked.
	RPI   time.Duration
	OTRPI time.Duration
	TORPI time.Duration
	// OutputFormat is the O->T real-time format: the zero value means the
	// 32-bit run/idle header, or heartbeat when OutputSize is 0.
	// InputFormat is the T->O format: the zero value is modeless.
	OutputFormat *implicit.Format
	InputFormat  implicit.Format
	// Class is the transport class, 1 (the zero value) or 0 (set
	// ClassZero).
	ClassZero bool
	// Multicast asks for the T->O data by multicast.
	Multicast bool
	// TimeoutMultiplier: the connections time out after RPI × 4 << n.
	// Default 0 (×4); at most 7.
	TimeoutMultiplier uint8
	// Large uses Large_Forward_Open; it is chosen automatically when a
	// connection size exceeds 511.
	Large bool
	// Key is the electronic key to put in the path; nil sends none.
	Key *cip.KeySegment
	// Reconnect, when set, reopens the connection after a timeout.
	Reconnect *Reconnect
	// Output is the output data sent from the first datagram on, OutputSize
	// octets; nil sends zeros until SetOutput. Idle starts the connection
	// in idle (FormatHeader32 only), so that a device does not act on
	// outputs before the application sets them and calls SetRun(true).
	Output []byte
	Idle   bool
	// OnInput is called with each new input (T->O) data and its run
	// state, on the endpoint's goroutine: it must not block. data is only
	// valid during the call.
	OnInput func(data []byte, run bool)
	// OnState is called when the connection's state changes.
	OnState func(ethernetip.State, error)
}
```

IOConfig describes an I/O connection.

WithEndpoint makes the scanner use an I/O endpoint it does not own, for example one shared by the scanners of several targets.

#### func WithLocalAddr

```go

```

WithLocalAddr sets the UDP address of the scanner's own endpoint; default ":2222".


WithLogger sets the logger.

#### func WithMulticastInterface

```go
func WithMulticastInterface(ifi *net.Interface) Option
```

WithMulticastInterface sets the interface the scanner's own endpoint joins multicast groups on (see [implicit.WithMulticastInterface](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/implicit#WithMulticastInterface)); by default the system chooses.

### type Scanner

```go
type Scanner struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Scanner opens I/O connections to the target of a client. It is safe for concurrent use.

#### func New

```go
func New(c *client.Client, opts ...Option) (*Scanner, error)
```

New returns a scanner of the target of c. Unless WithEndpoint is given, it opens its own I/O endpoint, which Close closes.

#### func (Scanner) Close

```go
func (s *Scanner) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close closes every connection of the scanner (with Forward\_Close, within ctx) and its own endpoint.

#### func (Scanner) Endpoint

```go
func (s *Scanner) Endpoint() *implicit.Endpoint
```

Endpoint returns the scanner's I/O endpoint.

#### func (Scanner) Open

```go
func (s *Scanner) Open(ctx context.Context, cfg IOConfig) (*IO, error)
```

Open opens an I/O connection with Forward\_Open and starts exchanging data: the output is OutputSize zero octets with run until SetOutput.
